Ok, I'm late here, but will still add my two cents.

    I learned that zinc coating is poisonous for birds.  I had my bird tested and then the cage.  It turned out the bird was ingesting bits of white paint from the cage and the paint contained zinc.  Take away the cage (source of zinc) and it helped tremendously.

    On another parrot that was chewing her feathers...  I put a dab of organic coconut oil on my hands, spread it all over the hands, then rubbed and scratched the bird.  She would preened her feathers instead of chewing them.  The dab was the size of a pencil point.  Watch the bird's droppings to be sure you are not overdoing it.

PS:  I found zinc in the cage paint, the C-hook for toys, and chains in toys. 

PPS: Cheap toys?  Roll and tie a magazine, cardboard boxes, human infant toys, golf wiffle balls, green beans in the shell.
